land.text: Dost Mohammad's Kabul and Ghazni: 'the British marched to Kabul with no resistance from Dost Mohammad's troops'; 'in August 1839, after thirty years, Shuja was again enthroned in Kabul'
Kandahar: 'Fall of Kandahar: 8 May 1839'; the page lists '1839: Durrani Empire (Shah Shuja)' as the principality's successor

predecessors.note: No dossier exists yet for the principality.

land.text: Kabul and Ghazni: Dost Mohammad's restoration in April 1843 ('Restoration: April 1843', Emirate infobox)

successors.note: The Emirate page: 'restoration, April 1843'. Kandahar left in August 1842 and is not part of the emirate's land until 1855 (emirate-of-afghanistan ledger).

land.text: Kandahar: 'Liberation of Kandahar: 9 August 1842'; 'They occupied Kandahar and re-established the principality.'

successors.note: No dossier exists yet for the principality; Kohan Dil Khan's reign there starts on 9 August 1842 (Principality of Kandahar page).

capitals.name: Kabul (Bala Hissar)
capitals.note: Shuja was 'again enthroned in Kabul' in August 1839; the British held the city until the Army of Retribution took it back in September 1842.

rulers.name: Shuja Shah Durrani
rulers.note: Second reign, 7 August 1839 to 5 April 1842, when he was assassinated (his first reign ran 1803-1809).

rulers.name: Fateh Jang
rulers.note: 5 April to 12 October 1842; 'fled with the British after their punitive expedition to Kabul, leaving in October 1842' (Durrani dynasty page).

rulers.name: Shahpur Shah
rulers.note: 12 October to December 1842 on the Durrani Empire page; the First Anglo-Afghan War page has his reign end 'with the return of Dost Mohammad Khan from exile' (April 1843).

region.text: Kabul and Ghazni, Dost Mohammad's land that the British put under Shuja

ledger.note: August 1839: Shuja Shah is enthroned at Kabul by the British. 'In August 1839, after thirty years, Shuja was again enthroned in Kabul'; the British had taken Kandahar on 25 April and Ghazni on 23 July. Durrani Empire page: Shuja Shah's second reign from 7 August 1839. The Kandahar lands (confidence 2) come from the Principality of Kandahar page. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: the Kandahar lands came from the Principality of Kandahar, not from the emirate, and are entered in the next event; the emirate dossier holds Kandahar out until 1855.]

region.text: Kandahar, the principality's land that the British put under Shuja

ledger.note: 1839: Kandahar passes to Shuja's state. The Principality of Kandahar infobox has 'Fall of Kandahar: 8 May 1839' and lists '1839: Durrani Empire (Shah Shuja)' as its successor (the page has no sentence on the 1839 capture; the First Anglo-Afghan War page has the British 'finally set up camps at Kandahar on 25 April 1839'). The land changed hands before Shuja's August enthronement at Kabul and is entered at the state's start. Kandahar is named by the page; Hilmand and Uruzgan are my reading of the principality's lands (the page names Uruzgan only for the Dil brothers' later division), hence confidence 2.

2 November 1841: the Kabul uprising. The chiefs met on the night of 1 November and 'the uprising began in the morning of the next day'; the British retreated from Kabul in January 1842 and Shuja was assassinated in April 1842.

region.text: Kandahar, liberated by the Dil brothers

ledger.note: 9 August 1842: Kandahar leaves. Principality of Kandahar infobox: 'Liberation of Kandahar: 9 August 1842', and Kohan Dil Khan's reign there starts that day; the article says of the Dil brothers 'They occupied Kandahar and re-established the principality.' The infobox lists '1842: Durrani Empire (Shah Shuja)' as the state the principality followed. First Anglo-Afghan War page: 'General William Nott advanced from Kandahar, capturing Ghazni and partially demolishing the city's fortifications' (August 1842) and 'Ellenborough ordered the forces at Kandahar and Jalalabad to leave Afghanistan.' Kabul and Ghazni stay with the state until April 1843. Region is Kandahar named by the page plus Hilmand and Uruzgan as in the gain. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: the 1843 loss and the dissolution had handed Kandahar to the emirate, which does not take it until 1855.]

October 1842: the Army of Retribution leaves. 'The combined British forces defeated all opposition before taking Kabul in September' and then 'withdrew from Afghanistan through the Khyber Pass'; Fateh Jang, 'leaving in October 1842', went with them; Shahpur Shah was left at Kabul until Dost Mohammad's return.

April 1843: Dost Mohammad returns. 'Restoration, April 1843' (Emirate infobox); Shahpur's reign 'ended with the return of Dost Mohammad Khan from exile in India' (First Anglo-Afghan War page). The Durrani Empire page puts Shahpur's end in December 1842 and the collapse of the restoration in April 1843. Kandahar had already left in August 1842 (previous loss, Principality of Kandahar page); the emirate takes Kabul and Ghazni only. [Repaired after review ia-03-e.]

April 1843: the British-backed Durrani restoration ends and Dost Mohammad resumes at Kabul. The Durrani house kept Herat to 1863 (Herat page, Kamran Shah's line) outside this dossier. Kandahar had already left in August 1842 (previous loss, Principality of Kandahar page); the emirate takes Kabul and Ghazni only. [Repaired after review ia-03-e.]

correction.text: Kabul, Ghazni and Kandahar, the lands the British held for Shuja Shah

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Durrani Dynasty row begins in 1840 but Shuja was enthroned at Kabul in August 1839 ('In August 1839, after thirty years, Shuja was again enthroned in Kabul'), after the British took Kandahar on 25 April and Ghazni on 23 July 1839. Shape: Kabul, Ghazni and the Kandahar principality's lands (Kandahar, Helmand, Uruzgan). Herat stayed with Kamran Shah and then Yar Mohammad Khan.

correction.text: Kabul and its 160 km circle (which takes in Jalalabad), Ghazni and the Kandahar lands: the land of the 1839 keyframe, held through 1840-1842

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1840 shape is 0.665 M km2 (664,591), the whole of modern Afghanistan, 99% of the country; the Durrani dynasty page gives no area. It is replaced by the land of the 1839 keyframe, about 0.21 M km2 on the grid (roughly a third): Kabul and its 160 km circle, which takes in Jalalabad ('held by a force which had been sent from Kabul in October 1841 as the first stage of a planned withdrawal', First Anglo-Afghan War page), Ghazni and the Kandahar lands. No page or event explains a gain of 0.4 M km2 between 1839 and 1840, and the state held only what the British garrisoned (certainty). The First Anglo-Afghan War page lists the Maimana Khanate and Tashqurghan (Khulm) as belligerents of their own and names no northern town under Shuja; the Shah Shuja Durrani page gives no territory for 1839-1842. So the north, Hazarajat and Herat are not drawn: unverified. Herat was a separate state ('Kamran was murdered in early 1842 on Yar Mohammad's orders', Herat page) and Kafiristan fell only in 1895-96. Dost Mohammad was exiled to India in November 1840 (Dost page: 'exiled by the British to Mussoorie in November 1840'); the Kabul uprising began on 2 November 1841. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: the 1840 keyframe was all of Afghanistan without Herat and Nuristan, 0.4 M km2 larger than the 1839 keyframe with no event.]

correction.text: Kabul and its 160 km circle and Ghazni: the year-end state of 1842, after Kandahar's liberation on 9 August 1842, held until April 1843

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria lists 0.666 M km2 for 1842-1845, the whole of modern Afghanistan; the restoration ended in April 1843: 'restoration, April 1843' (Emirate infobox), Dost Mohammad's second reign as Emir of Kabul from April 1843. Years 1843-1845 belong to emirate-of-afghanistan (keyframe emirate-of-afghanistan_1843). The shape holds for 1842 to April 1843 with Fateh Jang (April-October 1842) and Shahpur Shah, and is the year-end state: Kandahar, Hilmand and Uruzgan left on 9 August 1842 (ledger; Principality of Kandahar page 'Liberation of Kandahar: 9 August 1842'), so they are out of this shape, and the emirate's dossier takes Kandahar only in 1855. Ghazni stays with Kabul to April 1843 because no page hands it over. The north, Hazarajat and Herat are not drawn, as in 1840 (unverified). [Repaired after review ia-03-e.]

wars.name: First Anglo-Afghan War
wars.outcome: Barakzai victory (infobox): the British enthroned Shuja in August 1839, lost the Kabul uprising of 2 November 1841 and the retreat of January 1842, retook Kabul in September 1842 and withdrew in October; Dost Mohammad returned in April 1843.
wars.note: Dates for this state's life; the war itself began on 1 October 1838 (Simla Declaration).

certainty.note: The state held what the British garrisoned (Kabul, Ghazni and Jalalabad, with Kandahar until 9 August 1842); no frontier line is described, and the Sikh frontier at Peshawar and the Khyber is approximate.

notes: Cliopatria's Durrani Dynasty row (1840..1845) stands for Shuja Shah's British-backed restoration, which ran from August 1839 to April 1843 on the pages; the Wikipedia article 'Durrani dynasty' (Q5316729) is about the whole house (founded July 1747, dissolved 28 April 1856) and a redirect-free separate article, so this dossier is limited to the restoration and the Durrani Empire dossier carries 1747-1823. Cliopatria's 1843-1845 years belong to the Emirate of Afghanistan (Dost Mohammad restored April 1843); the Emirate dossier has the matching new keyframe. The reviewer may prefer to merge this dossier into emirate-of-afghanistan as a British-occupation interlude (rename plus occupation events) because the Barakzai emirate resumed on the same land; it is kept separate because Cliopatria and Wikidata keep the row apart and the ruling house differed. Pages disagree on the end: the Durrani Empire page has Shahpur Shah's reign end in December 1842 and the restoration collapse in April 1843; the Durrani dynasty page has Shuja deposed by Akbar Khan in 1842 (the First Anglo-Afghan War page has him assassinated; no month on that page). The British client relation (Shuja a vassal of the British Empire) and the occupation of 1839-1842 belong in the british-empire ledger; counterpart british-empire needs matching vassal_start and occupation events there. Not settled within the page budget: the Hindu Kush north, and whether Jalalabad and the Khyber approach counted as Shuja's land. The area check is impossible: the Durrani dynasty page gives no area. Repaired after review ia-03-e (2026-10-19): Kandahar, Hilmand and Uruzgan leave in August 1842 to the re-established Principality of Kandahar (loss event) and are no longer handed to the emirate in 1843; the Kandahar lands entered in 1839 come from the principality, not the emirate; the 1840 and 1842 keyframes are drawn from the 1839 land (the garrisoned lands) instead of all of Afghanistan, and the north, Hazarajat and Herat are unverified (the Shah Shuja Durrani and First Anglo-Afghan War pages name no northern town under Shuja).
